entities.summary: Aelius Donatus was a Roman grammarian and teacher of rhetoric who played a crucial role in the preservation and transmission of classical Latin literature during the Late Antique period. His extensive commentaries on the works of Cicero and Caesar, which were widely studied and emulated, helped shape the educational curriculum of the Roman Empire. Donatus's influence extended beyond his own time, with his works continuing to be studied and referenced in medieval and Renaissance Europe. The rediscovery of his commentaries in the 16th century sparked a renewed interest in classical Latin literature, contributing to the Renaissance humanist movement. Donatus's legacy is also reflected in the development of the medieval school of rhetoric, which emphasized the importance of clear and effective communication. Through his work, Donatus helped to shape the development of Western literature and education, leaving a lasting impact on the cultural and intellectual landscape of the Western world.
